cases.request: Turn this locked screenplay scene into shot cards for a 25-second sequence. Preserve the dialogue and story beats, but do not generate yet.
expect: Preserves locked scene intent and dialogue instead of performing an unsolicited screenplay rewrite
Defines shot intent, duration, exact participants, active references, geography, first frame, blocking, action, camera, audio, continuity, risk, and pass criteria
Chooses shot count and edit structure from dramatic purpose and production capability rather than a fixed template
Does not invoke a generation tool because the user requested planning only

cases.request: Generate an eight-second single take of Mara crossing the kitchen, hiding the knife behind her back, and answering Idris without breaking eye contact. Use the connected video model and these approved references.
expect: Seals the current shot with exact characters, prop ownership, location state, duration, active references, and continuity
Defines first-frame occupancy, spatial blocking, chronological action, camera behavior, physical contact, performance, exact dialogue, and sound
Inspects the connected tool schema and maps the prompt to supported fields rather than assuming a hardcoded provider
Waits for completion and inspects the actual returned clip before calling it finished

cases.request: Create a four-shot animated escape: wide geography, close reaction, mechanism insert, and vehicle departure. Use one generation only if the connected model can control all four shots reliably.
expect: Builds an edit-aware scene plan with independently runnable shot segments and explicit continuity
Inspects actual multi-shot and cut control rather than presuming support
Uses one generation only when the tool can reliably express the requested structure and otherwise returns or generates separate shots
Preserves reference roles, states, screen direction, audio, and leaving states across the edit

cases.request: Prompt this frame with exactly two named characters, one dog, and one red suitcase. Audit the six attached references and use only what this shot needs.
expect: States exact visible counts and identifies every active subject and important object
Assigns each used reference a declared role and removes stale or conflicting references
Uses positive occupancy and ownership constraints rather than relying on a generic no-duplicates list
Keeps unrelated characters, states, and source framing out of the current-shot context

cases.request: Design the first frame and blocking for the interrogation. The room reference controls geography, not composition. Niko begins beside the one-way mirror and Lena owns the folder.
expect: Maps stable landmarks and spatial relations independently of the source image composition
Defines frame-one occupancy, depth, facing, gaze, hands, contacts, prop ownership, camera side, and initial focus
Tracks paths and end positions in both screen-relative and world-relative terms where useful
Avoids an unintended empty opening and decorative blocking with no dramatic function

cases.request: Direct the camera so the hallway feels long and the watcher feels distant, then slowly reveal that he is closer than expected. Keep the provider configurable.
expect: Defines the observable framing, depth compression or expansion, subject relationship, and reveal before numeric lens syntax
Specifies camera start, side, height, path, speed, inertia, motivation, focus behavior, and end state
Maps to focal length, field of view, or camera presets only when the selected tool supports them
Avoids hardcoded cinematographer names, fashionable focal lengths, and stacked impossible moves

cases.request: Create a ten-second shot where a heavy steel door jams, the character throws her weight into it, the latch breaks, and she stumbles through. Make the contact and inertia believable.
expect: Builds a chronological trigger, effort, contact, failure, release, stumble, recovery, and final state
Describes weight transfer, grip, friction, resistance, latch failure, door mass, momentum, and physical consequence
Leaves enough duration for the requested mechanics and performance or reports a timing conflict
Carries the broken latch, open door, exertion, and end position into continuity

cases.request: The only strong source is the passing train outside. Light the room and let the character disappear into darkness after the final carriage passes.
expect: Defines the train as the motivated source with direction, movement, hardness, color, exposure, shadow, and environmental interaction
Times the lighting change to the physical passage of the train rather than a decorative fade
Preserves practical or ambient contributions only when their hierarchy remains coherent
Avoids universal backlight or flat-light rules that contradict the scene

cases.request: Prompt this two-character exchange. Only Asha speaks the exact line in Hindi; Tomas listens and keeps his mouth closed. Preserve Asha's voice identity and exhausted breath state.
expect: Locks exact text, language, speaker ownership, timing, voice identity, delivery, and physical breath state
Directs Tomas's listening and explicitly keeps his visible mouth silent without assigning him speech
Inspects dialogue, audio, voice-reference, lip-sync, and multi-character support in the actual tool
Provides a separate audio handoff when the video model cannot reliably satisfy the audio requirements

cases.request: Use this approved performance packet inside a six-second close shot. Do not change the objective, tactic shift, exact line, or leaving state; add only the video direction needed.
expect: Preserves the approved performance core rather than replacing it with generic emotional adjectives
Scales visible behavior and dialogue delivery to the six-second close framing
Adds only shot-specific blocking, camera, optics, timing, lighting, audio, and continuity direction
Reports any conflict between the approved acting, duration, blocking, and tool capability

cases.request: Plan a ten-second threshold transformation from the supplied closed and open armor references. The shoulder plates unlock, rotate, and seal after she crosses the doorway.
expect: Assigns the closed and open references to explicit visible states
Defines stable before-state, trigger, crossing, ordered mechanical motion, contacts, intermediate states, lock, and stable after-state
Tracks doorway geography, character blocking, mechanism scale, lighting, sound, and persistent final state
Splits or simplifies the shot if the selected model cannot reliably solve the transformation and crossing together

cases.request: Make the creature feel thirty meters tall in a street-level shot. The previous take just looked like a normal animal close to camera.
expect: Combines measurement with frame relation, familiar comparisons, environmental landmarks, and visible physical consequences
Uses blocking, camera clearance, perspective, movement, shadow, debris, or sound to prove scale
Diagnoses false proximity or missing environmental evidence instead of repeating only the number
Preserves the approved creature identity while changing the scale evidence

cases.request: Use my connected remote video service to generate shot 12B, wait for it, inspect it, and save the approved take to the project.
expect: Inspects the active connector, authentication, model, schema, reference limits, settings, cost, output, and project-write capabilities
Submits only the required current-shot material and tracks queued, processing, completed, and failed states accurately
Inspects the completed clip against the shot pass criteria before approving it
Saves only with authorization and records prompt version, job ID, asset ID, settings, inspection result, and take status

cases.request: Generate this scene in Claude web, but no video connector appears to be available.
expect: Confirms that no compatible tool is visible instead of pretending the skill grants generation access
Provides Claude-appropriate remote connector guidance, authentication, and tool verification
Returns a complete manual scene, shot, prompt, reference, settings, audio, edit, and verification package if connection cannot be completed
States clearly that no video was generated

cases.request: Show me how to connect my remote video MCP to ChatGPT web and Codex CLI before we upload any footage.
expect: Explains that ChatGPT web uses hosted plugin or connector tools and does not read local Codex MCP configuration
Provides the appropriate Codex remote MCP setup and status-verification path
Covers trusted endpoints, authentication, permissions, secrets, privacy, cost, tool-schema inspection, and a low-risk test
Does not upload footage or begin generation

cases.request: I have three video models connected. Choose one for a 16-second two-character dialogue shot that needs identity references, a controlled dolly, exact speech, and lip sync.
expect: Inspects actual tool schemas and model versions rather than relying on a hardcoded ranking
Compares reference fidelity, supported duration, camera control, exact dialogue, multi-speaker audio, lip sync, privacy, cost, and output
Explains any material tradeoff or asks only if the choice remains consequential
Suggests splitting picture and audio or the shot itself when no one model can reliably satisfy the full request

cases.request: Audit this Seedance-style prompt for use with a different video model. It contains stale tags, three contradictory camera moves, fixed field-of-view syntax, and a huge negative list. Do not generate.
expect: Separates provider-neutral scene direction from unsupported provider-specific syntax
Removes stale references and resolves contradictory camera behavior around one observable move
Converts optical intent into observable outcomes before adapting to the selected model
Replaces broad bans with positive shot-specific constraints and does not invoke a tool

cases.request: Inspect these chase clips for identity drift, duplicate riders, screen-direction breaks, weightless impacts, lighting resets, dead reactions, speaker mistakes, flicker, and unstable edges. Diagnose first.
expect: Inspects the actual media and supports findings with observable moments
Classifies source, prompt, complexity, continuity, capability, audio, performance, and stochastic artifact failures
Compares each shot's leaving state with the next shot's entering state
Does not regenerate because the user requested diagnosis first

cases.request: The shot is approved except the suitcase floats during the handoff. Fix only the contact and weight while preserving identity, framing, camera, acting, lighting, dialogue, and timing.
expect: Preserves all named accepted elements and identifies the suitcase handoff as the local failure
Reinforces hand ownership, contact, grip, weight transfer, inertia, and release in the relevant action phase
Uses an edit, localized revision, or controlled regeneration capability when available
Compares the revision against the accepted take and records exactly what changed

cases.request: Extend the approved train shot by three seconds until the final carriage clears frame. Keep the end-frame direction, rain, reflections, camera motion, ambience, and character state continuous.
expect: Uses the accepted output and canonical references with explicit extension continuity
Preserves motion phase, screen direction, weather, lighting, camera inertia, sound, and performance state
Defines the new final frame and edit-ready leaving state
Inspects the seam and the extended segment rather than assuming continuity from a successful job status

cases.request: Keep generating versions until the scene is perfect. The service charges per clip and I have not set a budget.
expect: Converts perfection into observable shot-specific pass criteria
Does not begin an unbounded paid generation loop
Requests or proposes a cost and retry boundary before additional paid generations while continuing safe planning work
Stops or redesigns when repeated attempts show no measurable improvement

cases.request: Prepare a model-neutral prompt-only package for this 12-second scene with active references, exact counts, first frame, blocking, camera, optics, timing, physics, lighting, performance, dialogue, audio, and pass criteria. Do not generate.
expect: Returns a signal-dense provider-neutral production prompt covering every relevant requested category
Includes reference roles, selected-provider adapter or capability assumptions, settings, attachment order, naming, continuity, and verification
Uses exact dialogue, positive constraints, present-tense observable action, and chronological timing
States clearly that no video was generated

cases.request: Package scenes 14 through 18 for the editor and another video-generation team. Include approved takes, rejected takes, prompt versions, audio, and continuity.
expect: Packages model profiles, scene plans, independent shot cards, prompts, reference registry, output registry, edit map, continuity log, audio package, take log, and open issues
Distinguishes locked creative facts from provider adapters and experiments
Labels accepted, rejected, superseded, queued, and unverified assets unambiguously
Creates a standalone handoff that does not require this skill or upstream skills to interpret

cases.request: help
expect: Explains scene planning, prompting, generation, revision, auditing, continuity, and connector execution without directing or generating a scene
Lists plan, create, revise, audit, prompt-only, and help modes
Provides a starter and another realistic example for every mode
Explains plan, prompt-only, generate, generate-and-refine, and manual-handoff choices plus connector boundaries

cases.request: Write the complete second act of this feature screenplay with scene headings and dialogue.
expect: Uses the screenwriting workflow rather than invoking video direction

expect: Uses the image-direction workflow rather than invoking video direction
